headline: Chennai shows slight warming, but not enough to call it yet
summary: Evidence gathered; it can’t yet be told apart from chance.
verdict: Inconclusive is a finding, not a failure. The evidence is on file; it just doesn’t clear the bar to rule out chance. We’d rather say so than overstate it.

evidence_notes.temp_trend: Chennai’s yearly average may have edged up slightly since 1981, but the signal fades once we allow for asking several questions of the same data.
evidence_notes.hot_days: Very hot days may be slightly fewer, but it isn’t a clear trend. That’s the opposite of what you’d expect, so it’s worth a second look.
evidence_notes.temp_shift: There may be a step up from 1997 onward (+0.21 °C vs. the years before), but it could be chance: a lead to follow, not a finding.
evidence_notes.global_context: For comparison: Earth as a whole warmed clearly and steadily over the same years.

suspects.description: Do drier months explain warm months? We line up rain and temperature month by month. A match would show they move together, not that one causes the other.
suspects.finding: Unclear: drier months line up only weakly with warmer ones (r = −0.21 in the same month), so rainfall explains little of the change.

devils_advocate: This data averages a ~50 km area and blends satellite and model inputs, so it can hide city-scale heat. The 1997 shift could reflect a natural swing or a change in the satellites feeding the model, not a real turning point.
devils_advocate_note: We keep this objection on the record. It is why the verdict stays Inconclusive.
can_say: Our best estimate for Chennai is +0.065 °C per decade, but that can’t yet be told apart from chance. Over the same years the whole planet warmed at +0.211 °C per decade.
what_data_cannot_tell_us: That Chennai’s trend is more than chance, or that 1997 was a real turning point (p = 0.17).
would_change_it: Sharper, city-scale evidence: MODIS satellite land temperature at 1 km.
next_witness: Sharper satellite evidence: MODIS land temperature at 1 km, in the night-heat case.
